run.rulesInOwnWords: 1) Start: masses [3,6,6,2,2,1] for chambers 1-6, all LARVAL, waste tally 0. Every halving/quartering rounds down. 2) Each cycle runs steps 1-5 in order, each step completed for all six chambers before the next. Step 1 Feeding: add the cycle's feed charge to each chamber; no limit enforced. Step 2 Carry-forward: go chamber 1 to 6 in order; if mass > holding limit (10,8,12,6,9,7), move the excess into the next chamber and set this one to its limit; excess from chamber 6 goes to waste. Excess passed down can cascade within the same pass. Step 3 Stage check on post-step-2 mass: LARVAL with mass >= pupation mark (7,6,9,5,7,5) becomes PUPAL; PUPAL with mass <= return mark (3,2,4,2,3,2) becomes LARVAL; otherwise unchanged; at most one change per chamber per cycle; record each change. Step 4 Metabolism/reabsorption: compute all amounts first from current mass and post-step-3 stage (LARVAL = floor(mass/4), PUPAL = floor(mass/2)); then apply simultaneously: each chamber loses its amount; LARVAL amounts go to waste; PUPAL amounts are added to chamber n-1 (chamber 1 PUPAL amount goes to waste). No limit enforced here; any over-limit mass is fixed only in the next cycle's step 2. Step 5 Moult: if the six-chamber total is strictly greater than 38, halve every chamber (round down), add all removed mass to waste, and record the cycle as a moult cycle; total of 38 or less does nothing. 3) Report after step 5 of cycle 5: end masses, end stages, all stage changes, moult cycles, waste tally, and balance check (start total + all feed = end total + waste).

run.notes: I ran the arithmetic in a short Python script (sim.py in the session scratchpad) and checked cycle 1 by hand. The script's first balance printout hardcoded the starting total as 18. The correct figure is 20, and with it the books balance at 114 = 114. In cycle 5 the total is exactly 38, so there is no moult because the rule needs more than 38. Chamber 2 ends at 10, above its holding limit of 8, after taking in reabsorbed mass in cycle 5. As the sheet says, that is never corrected.
